title: Impact of Crop Insurance Subsidy Reform on Agricultural Land Use

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
**Difference-in-Differences (DID)** is the appropriate method here. We have a treatment group (farms receiving favorable insurance terms) and a control group, with data from before and after the reform implementation. The key assumption is **parallel trends** - that treated and control farms would have followed similar trends in land use absent the policy reform. The DID estimator compares the change in planted acreage for treated farms before/after the reform to the change for control farms over the same period.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s40_data.csv")

# Basic DID regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)

# Print main results with robust standard errors
cat("=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===\n")
robust_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1")))
coef_summary <- summary(did_model)$coefficients
coef_summary[, 2] <- robust_se
coef_summary[, 3] <- coef_summary[, 1] / robust_se
coef_summary[, 4] <- 2 * pt(abs(coef_summary[, 3]), df = did_model$df.residual, lower.tail = FALSE)
print(round(coef_summary, 4))

cat("\nTreatment Effect (DID Coefficient):", round(coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(robust_se["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", 
    round(coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"] - 1.96 * robust_se["treat_x_post"], 4), ", ",
    round(coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"] + 1.96 * robust_se["treat_x_post"], 4), "]\n")

# Calculate percentage effect (since y is in logs)
pct_effect <- (exp(coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]) - 1) * 100
cat("Percentage increase in planted acres:", round(pct_effect, 2), "%\n")

# Robustness check 1: Fixed effects model
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 1: UNIT FIXED EFFECTS ===\n")
fe_model <- lm(y ~ factor(unit_id) + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
fe_robust_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(fe_model, type = "HC1")))
cat("Treatment Effect with Unit FE:", round(coef(fe_model)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(fe_robust_se["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")

# Robustness check 2: Pre-trend test (if multiple pre-periods exist)
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 2: PARALLEL TRENDS TEST ===\n")
pre_periods <- unique(data$period[data$post == 0])
if(length(pre_periods) > 1) {
    # Create period-specific treatment interactions for pre-periods
    data$period_treat <- data$treated * data$period
    trend_test <- lm(y ~ treated + factor(period) + period_treat, 
                    data = data[data$post == 0, ])
    trend_coef <- coef(trend_test)["period_treat"]
    trend_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(trend_test, type = "HC1")))["period_treat"]
    cat("Pre-trend coefficient:", round(trend_coef, 4), "\n")
    cat("Pre-trend p-value:", round(2 * pt(abs(trend_coef/trend_se), 
                                         df = trend_test$df.residual, lower.tail = FALSE), 4), "\n")
} else {
    cat("Only one pre-period available - cannot test pre-trends\n")
}

# Summary statistics
cat("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")
summary_stats <- data %>%
    group_by(treated, post) %>%
    summarise(
        n = n(),
        mean_y = mean(y),
        sd_y = sd(y),
        .groups = 'drop'
    )
print(summary_stats)

# Sample composition
cat("\nSample composition:\n")
cat("Total observations:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Treated units:", length(unique(data$unit_id[data$treated == 1])), "\n")
cat("Control units:", length(unique(data$unit_id[data$treated == 0])), "\n")
cat("Time periods:", length(unique(data$period)), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a **positive coefficient** on the treatment effect (treat_x_post), indicating that favorable crop insurance terms increase planted acreage. The magnitude should be economically meaningful - likely between **0.10-0.30 in log points** (corresponding to roughly 10-35% increase in acres planted). This is because better insurance reduces farmers' risk exposure, making them more willing to plant additional acres that might have been too risky without insurance coverage. The effect should be statistically significant if the policy reform was substantial enough to meaningfully alter farmers' risk-return calculations.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log acres planted between treated and untreated farms before and after the subsidy reform.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The subsidy reform led to an increase in the log of acres planted.
